sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-End Loose-Leaf Tea Service and Cultural Ceramic Salons

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-2 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier for AML/CFT; Ordonnance n° 2017-1164 du 12 septembre 2017 relative au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (as amended by Law n° 2019-486)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or passport-issuing authority
Competent public authority (e.g., utility provider or bank)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Founding Documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against French national sanctions lists, EU consolidated sanctions, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and PEP databases using automated tools

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: infogreffe.fr (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language using Latin alphabet; names must adhere to standard French spelling and grammatical rules
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Reserved professional titles such as 'banque' or 'assurance' without ministerial approval
Terms that could mislead consumers or be offensive
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, administrative appeal may be filed with the Tribunal de commerce within one month; name modification request possible if approved

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for low-risk service industries such as specialty tea lounges; a physical address for correspondence and tax purposes is required, with virtual offices commonly accepted if they meet RCS formalities
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk (estimated 2-5%) for unannounced on-site inspections for a non-regulated service business

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal services for SAS incorporation and due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard French SAS formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Energy Sovereignty

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address and compliance setup
Sanctions screening and PEP monitoring software

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II: general company provisions (Articles L. 210-1 et seq.) and simplified joint-stock company provisions (Articles L. 227-1 through L. 227-27); formation and registration procedures set out in Articles R. 123-1 et seq. and R. 224-1 et seq.; Code monetaire et financier (right-to-account) and Code de l'environnement (water and waste) apply as ancillary.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (commercial court registry) of the registered office, operating through the INPI Guichet Unique des Formalites d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration de constitution d'une societe par actions simplifiee (SAS) filed on the Guichet Unique, leading to registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Societes (RCS) and issuance of the extrait Kbis
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS; the capital is freely fixed by the articles of association. Where capital is subscribed in cash, at least 50% must be paid up at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. The paid-up portion must be deposited into a French bank account and blocked until the Kbis certificate is issued, after which it is released upon certification by the President.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF THE COMPANY MADE AT THE INCORPORATION MEETING HELD ON [DATE] AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE. The shareholders, deliberating on the constitution of the SAS, unanimously: (i) approve the subscription of [--N--] shares, totalling a share capital of EUR [--X--], of which at least 50% is declared paid on account; (ii) fix the registered office at [--ADDRESS--]; (iii) appoint [--NAME--] as President and legal representative of the company, with powers to carry out all formalities; (iv) authorize the President to sign the articles, the legal announcement, the registration declarations and the sectoral license applications; (v) acknowledge that no statutory auditor is required under Article L. 227-9-1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and signing the Articles of Association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Not required to file at this stage; drafted by counsel and signed by the founders; notarial deed only mandatory if real property is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French, including corporate name, legal form (SAS), share capital and par value, registered office, corporate purpose (specialty tea salon, loose-leaf tea service and beverage serving under NAF/APE 5630Z), duration of 99 years, founding President and powers, transfer-of-shares restrictions, and the beneficial-ownership declaration data. Each founder signs each page and the final page; powers of attorney must be formalized for any representative signatory.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of each founding shareholder
Full text of the articles of association
Power of attorney if a representative signs
Draft registered office address and occupancy proof outline
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commercial court clerk later objects to the corporate name or to a clause, amend the articles by signed directive, re-execute the corrected pages, and resubmit with an explanatory letter; for contributions in kind, obtain or supplement the statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) report before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal constitution notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal announcement journal (Journal d'Annonces Legales) accredited in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Insert a legally compliant announcement stating the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and the President's identity. The journal issues the attestation de parution, which is mandatory for the RCS filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement text contains errors or a mismatch with the final articles, publish a corrigendum announcement immediately and obtain a corrected attestation; the defective publication is cured by the corrected version dated no later than the RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the French bank account and depositing the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French licensed credit institution or authorized payment institution; the issuing bank provides the attestation de blocage des fonds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a company-in-formation bank account, transfer at least half of the cash capital, and instruct the bank to block the funds until presentation of the Kbis extract. Obtain the blocking certificate, the account opening certificate, and the AML/KYC confirmation from the bank.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and President
Proof of address of the registered office
AML/KYC forms and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account, invoke the right-to-an-account procedure before the Banque de France, which will designate a bank; the designated bank must issue the blocking certificate within the regulatory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the incorporation formalities on the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), forwarded to the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online declaration of incorporation of an SAS, select the NAF code 5630Z, upload the signed articles, publication attestation, bank blocking certificate, registered office occupancy proof, beneficial owner declaration, identity documents, and powers of attorney. Pay the state fees electronically and retain the receipt number.
required_dossiers: Publication attestation of the legal announcement
Proof of legal occupancy of the registered office
Identity documents of the President and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe issues a query (demande de complement), respond through the online portal within 15 days, curing the identified defects such as missing signature pages, unclear corporate purpose, or incomplete DCBE data; after a second refusal, petition the juge commis of the commercial court for an order to compel registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Kbis extract and business identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce and INSEE/INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the greffe opens the RCS entry, issues the extrait Kbis (official certificate of incorporation), and the company is assigned SIREN, SIRET, APE 5630Z, and VAT identifiers; Kbis is the sole legal proof of corporate existence and should be downloaded from the official register portal.
required_dossiers: No additional documents required from applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis data are incorrect, file a rectification request with the same greffe; if the greffe refuses, appeal to the President of the commercial court or the Court of Appeal within the applicable time limits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food business and beverage service declaration (salon de the, non-alcoholic)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Departementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) of the department where the salon is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the prior declaration of food business activity for on-site beverage serving and light food catering (SMR declaration) before opening. Implement and maintain a HACCP plan, staff hygiene training records, traceability registers, and a food-contact materials compliance statement. The recepisse of declaration must be displayed and made available for inspection.
required_dossiers: RCS Kbis extract of the SAS
Completed DDPP food business declaration form
Premises layout plan and equipment list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected or placed under observation, implement the corrective measures notified by the DDPP, submit a supplementary declaration with proof of compliance, and request a follow-up inspection; an unjustified adverse decision may be appealed before the administrative tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire safety inspection and civil defense clearance (ERP type N, 5th category)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Communal Commission de Securite (Mairie) and the Service Departemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an opening request with the premises plan, maximum public capacity, fire-extinguishing equipment, emergency exits, alarm system, and accessibility certificates. After the commission visit, obtain a favorable fire safety notice and the local authority's operating decision; maintain the register of safety controls.
required_dossiers: Structural load inspection for mezzanine or terrace
Electrical and gas installation verification certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commission issues an unfavorable opinion, serve a compliance undertaking and remedy the listed defects, then request a second visit within three months; until a favorable opinion is issued, the establishment may not lawfully receive the public.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Departementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) acting under DGCCRF supervision, jointly with the Mairie (Commission de Securite) for the physical premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Declaration d'exploitation d'un etablissement de vente de boissons et de restauration commerciale (salon de the) with the DDPP recepisse, and the ERP fire safety clearing decision (avis de la commission de securite) for a 5th-category type N establishment

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Regionale de l'Environnement, de l'Amenagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA in the ordinary case; the activity is not listed in the ICPE nomenclature for standard tearoom equipment. A declaration regime applies only if special installations exceed thresholds, e.g., refrigeration or air-conditioning circuits containing more than 500 kg of fluorinated greenhouse gases (ICPE title 4802) or significant greasy-waste processes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge must comply with the municipal sewage regulation (reglement d'assainissement); any non-domestic connection requires prior authorization under Article L. 1331-10 of the Code de l'environnement including installation of a grease trap (separateur de graisses). Emissions: VOC from cleaning and air-care products limited to product safety data sheets and applicable indoor air thresholds; ventilation systems checked to avoid odor nuisance. Waste: five-stream sorting under the AGEC law, separate collection of food bio-waste, and disposal only by licensed waste carriers with documented transfer slips; stormwater runoff maintained clean and directed to the public network if connected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: favorable inspection report from the communal Commission de Securite for a 5th-category type N ERP, covering extinguishers, emergency lighting, exits, alarm, and staff training. Structural load inspection: verification of mezzanine, terrace, or after-rigging elements to prove safe load capacity and operator accessibility. Occupational clearance: submission of the DUER to the DREETS, medical fitness of staff, first-aid equipment, electrical installation conformity, and safe food-handling workstations before opening.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal at impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French-resident entities obtain SIREN and SIRET identifiers from the INSEE registry upon incorporation. VAT registration (TVA identification number FR followed by 11 digits) is mandatory if annual turnover exceeds the applicable threshold; the process requires filing the registration declaration with the tax authorities, after which the VAT ID is assigned automatically without further election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not provide check-the-box elections or elective hybrid mismatch regimes. Taxation is strictly determined by legal form; SAS entities are subject to entity-level corporate income tax under the Code Général des Impôts with no elective options available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €77,700 for service-based activities (ISIC 5630); registration is required if annual turnover exceeds this threshold applicable to the business activity
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under the Facturation Électronique de Tiers regime for all B2B transactions since 1 October 2024, requiring compliant XML or PDF formats with embedded digital timestamps and stamps. Real-time reporting obligations apply via the PEPITES platform for qualifying enterprises; API integration with tax authorities is mandated for clearance, stamping, and compliance verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods to non-EU destinations or provision of services performed outside France for non-EU customers where the customer is not established in the EU and the service is not effectively used in the EU. Eligibility requires proof that the transaction constitutes an export and the customer is located outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of receipt of payment from non-EU entity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims of zero-rating on exports may result in penalties of up to 40% of the unreported VAT amount, interest surcharges, and potential criminal prosecution under French tax law. Retrospective clawback of zero-rated VAT with loss of refund rights and administrative sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: European Central Bank for euro monetary policy and the Banque de France as France's national central bank and reporting, payment-system, and certain foreign-exchange supervisory authority. The French Treasury Directorate General of the Treasury, the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution, the Autorité des Marchés Financiers, the European Commission, and applicable EU sanctions authorities also regulate relevant banking, payment, capital-market, and foreign-exchange activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to EU and French anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax, customs, prudential, and financial-market rules. A French SAS may generally receive foreign investment, maintain euro and foreign-currency accounts, convert funds, pay foreign suppliers, distribute dividends, repay shareholder loans, and remit profits without a general prior foreign-exchange approval. Banks must verify the origin, purpose, beneficial ownership, economic rationale, and sanctions status of transactions. Dividend and other profit remittances require distributable profits, properly approved corporate accounts, withholding-tax analysis, treaty or EU relief documentation where applicable, and evidence that the payment is not an unlawful return of capital or prohibited financial assistance. Capital contributions and shareholder loans should be supported by subscription, loan, board, and accounting documents. Cash and payment-service restrictions, tax reporting, customs controls, and beneficial-owner disclosure obligations remain applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory obligation requiring a resident company to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, no general mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline for converting or repatriating commercial export receipts. Export proceeds may generally be held in euro or foreign-currency accounts and converted at the company's discretion, subject to contractual banking terms and applicable law. Export documentation, VAT and customs records, invoices, shipping evidence, payment records, accounting books, and transfer-pricing support must be retained under applicable French and EU requirements. Banks may request transaction-purpose information, commercial contracts, customs documents, and explanations of unusual balances. EU and French sanctions, anti-evasion, tax, customs, and anti-money-laundering rules may restrict particular counterparties or destinations. This assessment should be reconfirmed if France adopts emergency capital controls or if a transaction involves a sanctioned jurisdiction or regulated financial product.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account for SAS formation or capital increase, followed by an operational current account with euro SEPA access, foreign-currency capability, cards, merchant acquiring, and treasury services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account and operational current account with domestic payment, acquiring, trade-finance, and foreign-exchange services
Capital deposit account and operational current account with SEPA, SWIFT, card acquiring, foreign-currency, hedging, and trade-finance facilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group bank, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne entity selected for the business location
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account and operational current account with local collection, card acquiring, SEPA, foreign-currency, and working-capital facilities

Operational business current account with euro payment services and selected merchant and international-payment capabilities; capital-deposit availability must be confirmed for the relevant SAS formation process

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for euro collections, SEPA credit transfers, cards, expense management, and limited foreign-currency conversion, provided the provider is an EU-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution operating in France through passporting or an approved French framework. An EMI account is not a bank deposit and generally does not provide deposit-guarantee protection; safeguarded funds and client-money arrangements apply under the provider's licence. It may be unsuitable as the sole account for SAS capital formation, cash-intensive activity, merchant-acquiring settlement, large shareholder funding, trade finance, or transactions involving higher-risk jurisdictions. Offshore digital EMIs without EU authorisation, French passporting, or an appropriate local regulatory basis should not be used for regulated payment services to the SAS. The company must verify the provider's legal entity, licence, safeguarding model, service terms, settlement currencies, transaction limits, sanctions policy, and account-closure procedures.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not generally require all SAS directors or shareholders to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding, electronic signatures, certified identification, video verification, and document uploads may be accepted, particularly for low-risk structures. A bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, live video interview, French or EU address evidence, certified translations, specimen signatures, or a local representative. The legal representative, all ultimate beneficial owners, controlling persons, authorised signatories, and relevant parent entities must be identified. For SAS capital deposit accounts, the bank normally requires formation documents and may release the capital only after evidence of registration and delivery of the Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence. Non-resident ownership is permitted, but remote onboarding is discretionary and is more difficult where the ownership chain, source of funds, business activity, or payment geography is complex.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent SAS formation file, unavailable Kbis extract, unregistered address, unclear registered office, or mismatch between corporate documents and bank application
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent articles of association; certificate of incorporation or Kbis extract; registered-office evidence; board or shareholder resolution approving the account and signatories; identity and address evidence for directors, signatories, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners; ownership chart; business registration and tax identifiers; capital-subscription and deposit evidence; certified translations where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain, nominee shareholders, trust arrangements, bearer-like interests, or inability to identify the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ownership and control chart to each natural-person UBO; shareholder register; constitutional documents for every intermediate entity; certificates of incorporation and incumbency; UBO declarations; trust or foundation instruments where relevant; governing resolutions; notarised or certified documents where required; explanation of control rights and economic ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of capital, shareholder loans, cash injections, or funds originating from unrelated third parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital subscription agreement; shareholder-loan agreement; bank statements; audited or management accounts; sale or investment agreements; tax returns; dividend records; proof of accumulated income or asset sale; investor KYC; payment trail from the beneficial owner; written explanation connecting source of wealth, source of funds, and the proposed business activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Specialty tea, lounge, hospitality, or retail activity involving substantial cash receipts, late-night operations, alcohol, tobacco, gaming-like products, or unexplained cash-intensive turnover
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; premises lease; licence and permit schedule; expected monthly transaction volumes; cash-handling and cash-deposit policy; point-of-sale and merchant-acquiring contracts; supplier invoices; menu and product catalogue; VAT and accounting process; staff and operating model; explanation of any alcohol or regulated-product activity; independent cash-flow forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to or from high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned territories, politically exposed persons, or counterparties with adverse media
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty ownership and sanctions screening; contracts and invoices; shipping, customs, and delivery evidence; end-use statement; beneficial-owner identification; source-of-funds evidence; sanctions legal review; documented commercial rationale; approval workflow; evidence that no prohibited intermediary, bank, vessel, or destination is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity inconsistent with a low-risk French specialty-tea profile, including high-value transfers, rapid pass-through funds, multiple unrelated currencies, virtual assets, or unusual personal-account usage
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year or launch-period financial forecast; transaction-flow map; expected counterparties and countries; treasury policy; bank-account segregation policy; explanation of currency exposure; supplier and customer concentration analysis; prohibition on personal-account use; internal approval matrix; accounting and reconciliation procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax, VAT, customs, or beneficial-owner filing gaps, including unexplained discrepancies between banking activity, invoices, tax returns, and statutory accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax-registration evidence; VAT filings; customs declarations where applicable; statutory accounts; management accounts; invoices; payment reconciliations; transfer-pricing documentation where relevant; beneficial-owner register evidence; accountant confirmation; remediation plan for any historical discrepancy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person, senior public official, family member, or close associate connected to the ownership or management
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP identification and relationship disclosure; enhanced source-of-wealth and source-of-funds file; independent adverse-media review; senior-management approval; expected-activity monitoring plan; evidence of lawful tax and commercial origin of funds; periodic review schedule.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in share capital through a regulated French bank or other institution expressly accepted for SAS capital deposits into a designated capital deposit account. Use a clearly identified shareholder or parent account, not an unexplained third-party account. Provide the subscription agreement, articles, shareholder or board resolution, ownership chart, UBO evidence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, payment instruction, and bank reference identifying the transfer as share capital or shareholder funding. For an EU euro transfer, use SEPA Credit Transfer where available; for non-SEPA or non-euro transfers, use SWIFT with complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary, purpose, and UBO information. France generally has no statutory foreign-exchange purpose-code regime equivalent to controlled-currency jurisdictions; use an accurate payment narrative such as 'paid-in share capital', 'capital increase', or 'shareholder loan', and comply with the bank's internal purpose-code and regulatory-reporting fields. The bank may hold or reject funds pending verification. After registration, provide the Kbis extract and request release or reclassification of the capital deposit into the operational account. Reconcile every incoming transfer to the subscription ledger and retain the full audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers within the SEPA area, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT cross-border transfers, normally with MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA currencies or destinations; include accurate originator, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, contract, and purpose information. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, including irrevocable and, where appropriate, confirmed commercial LCs, for higher-risk suppliers or material shipments; define Incoterms, documentary conditions, inspection requirements, insurance, discrepancy handling, and sanctions representations. Documentary collections, open-account payments, and supplier prepayments should be approved according to counterparty and country risk. For imported tea, ceramics, packaging, and equipment, retain purchase orders, invoices, customs declarations, transport documents, certificates of origin, food-safety records where relevant, and proof of delivery. Ensure VAT, customs, sanctions, anti-bribery, and anti-money-laundering controls are aligned with the payment. Merchant-card receipts should settle into the French operational account through an acquiring institution and be reconciled to point-of-sale reports, refunds, chargebacks, and VAT records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorised bank or regulated investment firm, used to hedge documented commercial exposures and subject to MiFID II conduct, suitability or appropriateness requirements where applicable, contractual documentation, valuation, collateral, and EMIR obligations.

Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management or currency conversion, subject to authorised-counterparty requirements, documented underlying exposure, treasury approvals, valuation, and applicable EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation rules.

Currency options, including purchased vanilla options and documented option strategies, where commercially justified and approved under the company's risk policy; avoid uncovered speculative structures and obtain clear disclosure of premium, settlement, collateral, and maximum-loss characteristics.

Non-deliverable forwards may be used for currencies subject to delivery restrictions or where the counterparty offers a lawful regulated product, but they are generally less relevant to ordinary euro trade exposures. They must be transacted with an authorised counterparty, linked to a genuine exposure, documented under appropriate master terms, and assessed for EMIR, MiFID II, conduct, collateral, and reporting requirements.

Exchange-traded or centrally cleared currency futures may be used through an authorised broker or clearing member, subject to margining, daily mark-to-market, clearing, accounting, and liquidity requirements.

The SAS should prohibit speculative dealing, require board-approved counterparty limits, maintain a hedge register, document the hedged item and hedge ratio, segregate front-office approval from settlement, conduct periodic valuation and effectiveness testing, and obtain accounting advice for French GAAP or IFRS hedge accounting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or sole shareholder of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential judicial injunction and daily penalty; failure to file approved accounts may result in a fine of approximately EUR 1,500, increased to approximately EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance. No fixed automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe of the competent Commercial Court through the INPI single filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts, or two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial injunction, potential civil and criminal liability of the legal representative, and approximately EUR 1,500 fine, increased to approximately EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance. France has no prescribed automatic annual administrative strike-off deadline for this filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and appendices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for calendar-year taxpayers, subject to the annual electronic filing schedule; generally within three months after year-end for non-calendar year-ends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month and a 10% surcharge, with increased surcharges for prolonged or deliberate non-compliance; tax reassessment and enforcement may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual review of beneficial ownership and corporate information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; INPI single filing portal for any required amendment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standalone annual confirmation filing. Review at least annually and file changes generally within 30 days of the relevant event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare or update beneficial ownership information may trigger formal notice, judicial measures, fines, and restrictions affecting the entity's registry compliance. No automatic annual strike-off timetable is prescribed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local economic contribution assessment and payment, including CFE where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is generally payable by 15 December; initial CFE declaration obligations may arise during the first operating year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, collection surcharges, and compulsory recovery measures may apply. The amount depends on the commune, premises, tax base, and applicable exemptions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory where the SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million turnover excluding tax, or 50 average employees. Additional mandatory-audit rules may apply to certain parent, subsidiary, or controlled-group structures.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority framework. IFRS may be used in limited statutory circumstances but is not the default framework for an ordinary French SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation. The company must conduct an annual internal verification of ownership and control information and file amendments generally within 30 days after a change. Share transfers must be recorded in the securities movement register and shareholder accounts; applicable transfer tax formalities generally arise within one month.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or individual shareholder accounts
Register of corporate decisions and minutes
Records identifying the president, officers, and any statutory auditor
Beneficial ownership documentation and supporting evidence

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 350-1,650 per year, depending on location, mail handling, domiciliation services, and compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,200-10,800 per year for a standard SAS statutory audit; no statutory audit fee applies where an auditor is not legally required and none is voluntarily appointed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate. A qualifying small enterprise may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to the statutory ownership, turnover and paid-up-capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% SME rate applies to qualifying companies whose annual turnover does not exceed EUR 10 million, whose capital is fully paid up, and whose capital is held at least 75% by individuals or qualifying entities. French tax losses generally carry forward without a fixed expiry, subject to the annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the preceding financial year and capped at the lower of the preceding year's profit or EUR 1 million. The requested five-year parameter is not the general French loss carryforward rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, Corporate Income Tax Return, with annexes 2065 bis-SD and the relevant results and balance-sheet schedules, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal espace professionnel on impots.gouv.fr using EFI or through an accredited EDI provider. The SAS must also file the applicable liasse fiscale, ordinarily forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD under the normal regime or forms 2033-A-SD to 2033-G-SD under the simplified regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax installments are generally payable quarterly, with a fourth-quarter installment not required where the preceding year's corporate income tax was below the applicable statutory threshold. VAT, payroll and social-security filings are separate obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return and tax package are generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the standard filing deadline is the second business day after 1 May of the following year. The electronic payment of the final balance is generally due by the applicable filing deadline. Corporate income tax installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax service reference, financial year opening and closing dates, principal activity and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer. The French SAS files as a French tax-resident company on its worldwide French-taxable results, subject to applicable treaty allocation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable profit or tax loss calculated from the commercial accounts after tax adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, provisions, depreciation adjustments and tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign profits not legally attributable to the French company unless French transfer-pricing, permanent-establishment, controlled-entity or anti-abuse rules require inclusion. Maintain supporting accounting and tax-reconciliation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer the tax result from the relevant liasse fiscale schedule and distinguish current-year profit from utilized and carried-forward tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document any cross-border management charges, royalties, interest, procurement fees or shareholder expenses using arm's-length evidence and proof of services or financing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 25% standard rate or the 15% SME rate where all statutory conditions are satisfied, then deduct eligible tax credits and installments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent does not itself obtain the French SME rate. The rate is tested at the French SAS level, including qualifying ownership and capital conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065 bis-SD, distributions and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report distributions, deemed distributions, tax credits and other information required by the form and applicable annexes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record distributions to non-resident shareholders separately and verify dividend withholding, treaty eligibility, beneficial ownership and required residence documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File the balance sheet, income statement, fixed-asset schedules, provisions, depreciation, tax reconciliation, related-party information and loss schedules required by the selected tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile statutory accounts to tax accounts and retain invoices, contracts, payment evidence, inventory records, payroll records and related-party support in French or with reliable translations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose specified categories of expenses paid to related entities, including certain commissions, royalties, financial charges, management fees and other remuneration, where the statutory conditions and thresholds apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include reportable payments to foreign group companies and maintain the agreement, benefit evidence, calculation methodology and withholding-tax analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit the annual transfer-pricing declaration where the statutory conditions apply and maintain simplified or full documentation as required by French law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign related parties, transaction categories, values, jurisdictions, methods and adjustments. A small standalone tea salon may fall below documentation thresholds but remains subject to the arm's-length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pay corporate income tax, installments and balance electronically through the professional tax account; ensure the bank mandate and account details are valid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign ownership does not remove the French company's electronic payment obligation. Late payment remains chargeable even where the annual return was filed on time.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% after a formal notice is not complied with and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent maneuvers or abusive conduct. Late payment generally attracts a 5% payment surcharge plus late-payment interest currently calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory exceptions and changes. Tax fraud may trigger criminal prosecution, fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic French withholding rate on dividends and similar distributions paid to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and treaty reductions. The EU Parent-Subsidiary regime may eliminate withholding where the statutory conditions are met, commonly including qualifying EU ownership, a minimum 10% holding, minimum holding-period requirements or an appropriate commitment, subject-to-tax status and anti-abuse compliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the shareholder's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, legal-form and subject-to-tax conditions, confirm the applicable France tax treaty article and complete the French administrative forms or treaty-relief procedure applicable to the payment. Where immediate relief is unavailable, withhold at the domestic rate and seek a refund using the prescribed French tax authority process. Retain ownership charts, share registers, residence certificates, treaty forms, declarations, payment records and anti-abuse evidence. Treaty relief is not available merely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound French royalties and similar payments for use of intellectual property are generally subject to a 25% domestic withholding rate under the applicable statutory provisions, subject to treaty limitation, EU directives and exemptions. Outbound interest is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, subject to specific statutory exceptions, anti-abuse rules and payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 10% and interest withholding to 0% to 10%, but the exact rate depends on the payee's jurisdiction, beneficial ownership and treaty article. Payments must also be tested for deductibility, transfer pricing, interest limitation, hybrid mismatch and anti-conduit rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full French transfer-pricing documentation, including Local File and Master File concepts, is generally mandatory where the French entity's pre-tax turnover or gross assets is at least EUR 400 million, where it belongs to a group meeting the relevant EUR 400 million threshold, or where another statutory group or ownership condition applies. A French entity below the threshold remains subject to the arm's-length principle and may be required to provide simplified documentation and transaction evidence during an audit. The annual transfer-pricing declaration applies under separate statutory thresholds and conditions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate general economic substance regulation equivalent to the UAE ESR regime. Substance is nevertheless relevant under the French anti-abuse doctrine, treaty principal-purpose and beneficial-owner analysis, EU anti-avoidance rules, controlled foreign company rules, transfer-pricing requirements, hybrid mismatch rules and abuse-of-law principles. The SAS should maintain real French decision-making, premises, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, commercial risk control, accounting records and business rationale proportionate to its specialty tea lounge activity. A conduit entity, artificial management-fee chain or debt structure lacking commercial substance may be denied treaty relief or deductions and may trigger reassessment and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, maintaining parallel cash records, issuing false invoices, deducting personal or fictitious expenses, suppressing taxable receipts or deliberately falsifying accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, surcharges generally ranging from 40% to 80%, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with enhanced penalties in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS normally shields shareholders and directors from ordinary corporate debts, but directors may incur personal civil liability for management faults, tax-fraud participation, asset diversion or insolvency misconduct. Criminal liability is personal; imprisonment, criminal fines, professional prohibitions and judicial restrictions may apply. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require a specific judicial or enforcement basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to issue compliant receipts or invoices, suppressing point-of-sale transactions, underreporting dine-in or takeaway sales, misclassifying VAT rates, claiming unsupported input VAT or using undeclared cash.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, interest, applicable tax surcharges, penalties for inaccurate or fraudulent returns, possible seizure or closure measures in serious cases, and criminal prosecution where intentional fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who personally organizes or knowingly approves VAT fraud may be criminally liable and may face director-liability proceedings, tax-payment liability under applicable French rules and disqualification from management. Corporate protection does not protect deliberate personal participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Employing staff without required declarations, concealing working hours, paying off-book wages, misclassifying employees as contractors, failing to withhold payroll taxes or breaching mandatory health and safety rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back payment of wages, social contributions, payroll taxes and interest; administrative and criminal penalties for travail dissimulé; loss of public subsidies and procurement eligibility; and possible business closure or exclusion measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director or de facto manager may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, management bans and liability for unpaid contributions where statutory conditions are met. Directors may also be liable for employee claims if insolvency or deliberate misconduct is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and non-arm's-length related-party charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excessive royalties, management fees, shareholder expenses, interest or procurement charges; unsupported services; profit diversion to a foreign affiliate; or failure to provide required documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment, denial of deductions, withholding-tax exposure, interest, documentation penalties and applicable surcharges. France may also apply transfer-pricing penalties for failure to provide required documentation or declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil or criminal liability where they knowingly participate in fraudulent profit diversion, false invoicing or abuse of corporate assets. Ordinary tax adjustment alone does not automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Beneficial ownership, treaty abuse and shell-company conduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal recipient to obtain treaty benefits, routing dividends or royalties through a conduit, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, fabricating substance or misrepresenting tax residence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, collection of withholding tax, interest, 40% or 80% tax surcharges where applicable, abuse-of-law consequences and possible criminal fraud charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly submit false treaty documentation or implement a sham arrangement may face personal criminal and civil consequences, including fines, imprisonment in aggravated cases and management disqualification. Travel bans require a specific judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash, structuring payments, disguising the source of funds, failing to identify customers or beneficial owners where required, ignoring suspicious transactions or breaching professional reporting obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative enforcement, transaction restrictions, confiscation, criminal money-laundering penalties and severe fines. Cash-payment limits applicable to professionals and consumers must be observed; the general professional cash-payment limit is EUR 1,000, subject to statutory exceptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Knowingly facilitating laundering may result in personal criminal liability, imprisonment, fines, confiscation and management restrictions. Failure to implement reasonable controls may expose the director to regulatory and civil consequences even without proof of the underlying predicate offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed alcohol, food-safety or public-premises operation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling alcohol without the required licence, operating outside the declared premises or activity, failing mandatory food-hygiene controls, serving unsafe products or breaching opening, noise, occupancy or public-health requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative closure, licence suspension or withdrawal, fines, product seizure and criminal penalties for serious food-safety or licensing breaches.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and operational manager may be prosecuted personally for intentional or negligent breaches. Insurance coverage may be impaired where mandatory licences or safety procedures were absent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Distribution while insolvent or abuse of corporate assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends without distributable profits, making disguised distributions, transferring assets to shareholders, repaying related parties preferentially or continuing to trade while knowingly insolvent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invalidation or recovery of distributions, repayment claims, tax reassessment, insolvency clawback, liability for insufficiency of assets and possible bankruptcy-related criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for an insufficiency of assets, management bans, personal contribution claims and criminal liability for misuse of corporate assets or fraudulent bankruptcy. The corporate veil may be disregarded only on legally established grounds, not merely because the company has tax debts.
